name: Grand Rapids Chair Company

about:
Grand Rapids Chair Company is based in Byron Center, Michigan, a suburb of Grand Rapids. The business traces its roots to 1991 when Dave and Jill Miller founded Manufacturer's Resource as a contract furniture sales company. By the late 1990s their son Geoff had joined the family operation, and the Millers shifted from representing other brands to designing and building their own seating and tables, renaming the firm Grand Rapids Chair Company. Geoff assumed leadership in 2012 and today the company employs roughly 150 people.

The company manufactures commercial-grade seating and tables in its West Michigan factory. Production spans woodworking with solid hardwoods, metal fabrication in steel and aluminum, powder coating in more than 150 standard colors, and upholstery using high-performance textiles. An extensive fabric library and customizable finishes allow specifiers to tailor each piece. The factory's local footprint supports short lead times and the ability to fulfill one-off custom orders at volume-friendly pricing.

Grand Rapids Chair serves the restaurant, office, hospitality, and higher-education markets. Its product range includes chairs, stools, benches, lounge seating, communal and occasional tables, pedestal and T-base tables, and outdoor collections. Design partners and specifiers work with the company's in-house team and a network of independent industrial designers to outfit cafés, corporate hubs, hotel lobbies, and campus gathering spaces.

The Millers frame the business around a family mindset that values human connection. That philosophy extends to community involvement, such as the Brooke Chair—named for a family member with type 1 diabetes—which donates a portion of sales to the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation. The company says its differentiators are Michigan-made manufacturing, an industry-leading warranty, deep customization capability, and a people-first culture that aims to make every project frictionless.
